findings.meaning: For substates 10, 13 and 14 the arbitration phase does nothing; only substate 12 has a real decision handler. A port must still CALL them (the table is dense) but they are empty. Substate 12 is the only one of the four that re-evaluates anything per frame.

verdict.why:
NARROW REFUTATION. The instruction-level claim survives my independent re-derivation completely; one sentence of the MEANING is contradicted by real instructions.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (PROVEN, re-derived independently):
- `table 0x8010c88c 16 --bin EMZ0.BIN` gives [10]->0x80104174, [13]->0x80104920, [14]->0x80104d6c. Cited addresses are real.
- `bytes` at all three: `08 00 e0 03 00 00 00 00` = 0x03e00008 (jr ra) + 0x00000000 (nop). `dis` agrees:
    80104174: jr ra / 80104178: nop
    80104920: jr ra / 80104924: nop
    80104d6c: jr ra / 80104d70: nop
  DELAY-SLOT CHECK: the only branch in each function is the `jr ra`; its delay slot is a literal zero word, not a hidden instruction. Nothing to mis-assign. The EXECUTOR table entries sit exactly 8 bytes later (0x8010417c / 0x80104928 / 0x80104d74), which is independent corroboration that these functions are 2 instructions long.
- I ALSO strengthened the claim beyond what the agent showed: the dispatcher @0x8010118c DISCARDS the decision's return value, so "empty == truly inert" is airtight rather than merely plausible:
    801011c4: jalr v0            ; decision[+0x5]
    801011c8: addu s2,a2,zero    ; DELAY SLOT (executes)
    801011cc: addu a0,s0,zero
    801011d0: lbu v0,5(s0)       ; v0 CLOBBERED -> decision's v0 is never read
    801011e4: lw v0,-14132(at)   ; 0x8010c8cc executor table, indexed by the RE-READ +0x5
    801011ec: jalr v0
    801011f0: addu a2,s2,zero    ; DELAY SLOT (executes)
  So the decision phase's ONLY channel is writing +0x5; an empty body genuinely means "no arbitration this frame". Confirmed.
- EXECUTOR[10] @0x8010417c, EXECUTOR[13] @0x80104928, EXECUTOR[14] @0x80104d74 are all real functions (`addiu sp,sp,-40 / -56 / -32` frames). So "the logic is in their executors" holds.

WHAT FAILS - the final MEANING sentence: "Substate 12 is the only one of the four that re-evaluates anything per frame."
That is false as written. Substates 10 and 14 re-evaluate state and TRANSITION every frame, just in the executor rather than the decision. Contradicting instructions:

EXECUTOR[10] @0x8010417c runs a per-frame nested 5-way FSM on +0x6:
  801041b4: lbu v1,6(s1)
  801041c0: sltiu v0,v1,0x5
  801041c4: beq v0,zero,0x8010437c
  801041c8: sll v0,v1,2            ; DELAY SLOT (executes)
  801041d4: lw v0,228(at)          ; jump table @0x801000e4
  801041dc: jr v0
...and it decrements a per-frame timer and transitions on expiry:
  80104354: lhu v1,344(s1)
  8010435c: addiu v0,v1,-1
  80104360: bne v1,zero,0x8010437c
  80104364: sh v0,344(s1)          ; DELAY SLOT (store happens on BOTH paths)
  80104368: addiu v0,zero,4
  8010436c: j 0x8010437c
  80104370: sb v0,6(s1)            ; DELAY SLOT -> +0x6 = 4
...and it transitions off a per-frame turn result:
  80104254: jal 0x80015714
  80104258: andi a1,a1,0xfff       ; DELAY SLOT
  8010426c: bne v0,zero,0x8010437c
  80104270: sh v1,118(s1)          ; DELAY SLOT
  80104274: addiu v0,zero,2
  80104278: j 0x8010437c
  8010427c: sb v0,6(s1)            ; DELAY SLOT -> +0x6 = 2

EXECUTOR[14] @0x80104d74 likewise re-evaluates per frame:
  80104d90: lbu v1,6(s0)
  80104d98: beq v1,zero,0x80104db4
  80104d9c: addu s2,a2,zero        ; DELAY SLOT
  80104da4: beq v1,v0,0x80104dd0   ; v0=1
  80104dd0: lbu v1,333(s0)
  80104dd8: bne v1,v0,0x80104e0c   ; v0=10, per-frame compare

SECOND HAZARD - "only substate 12 has a real decision handler" is true only if silently scoped to {10,12,13,14}; unscoped it is false and contradicts this project's own established facts (DECISION[1]=0x80101714 is the real WALK decision). I dumped the first 2 instructions of ALL 16 decision entries: REAL = [0] 0x80101294, [1] 0x80101714, [2] 0x80101f7c, [12] 0x8010460c (all `addiu sp,sp,-40/-32`). STUBS (`jr ra; nop`) = [3] 0x801025e4, [4] 0x80103170, [5] 0x80103180, [6] 0x8010394c, [7] 0x80103778, [8] 0x80103b6c, [9] 0x80103e40, [10] 0x80104174, [11] 0x80104394, [13] 0x80104920, [14] 0x80104d6c, [15] 0x80104e4c. 12 of 16 are stubs, not 3.

NOT CLAIMED / STILL UNKNOWN: I did not establish what substates 10/13/14 mean, nor that they are ever entered at runtime. That was not asserted, so it is not part of the refutation.
verdict.correction:
KEEP (PROVEN, verified byte-exact by me): DECISION[10] @0x80104174, DECISION[13] @0x80104920 and DECISION[14] @0x80104d6c are 2-instruction empty functions — `jr ra` (0x03e00008) + `nop` (0x00000000). Their EXECUTOR counterparts begin exactly 8 bytes later at 0x8010417c / 0x80104928 / 0x80104d74. Calling them is a true no-op because the dispatcher @0x801011c4 `jalr v0` never reads the returned v0 — it is clobbered at `801011d0: lbu v0,5(s0)` before the executor index is computed. A port may call empty stubs or skip them; behavior is identical.

ADD (PROVEN, the agent under-reported this): the stub pattern is the RULE, not a 3-entry exception. Of the 16 upright decision handlers, only FOUR are real: [0] 0x80101294, [1] 0x80101714, [2] 0x80101f7c, [12] 0x8010460c. The other TWELVE are all `jr ra; nop`: [3] 0x801025e4, [4] 0x80103170, [5] 0x80103180, [6] 0x8010394c, [7] 0x80103778, [8] 0x80103b6c, [9] 0x80103e40, [10] 0x80104174, [11] 0x80104394, [13] 0x80104920, [14] 0x80104d6c, [15] 0x80104e4c. So "only substate 12 has a real decision handler" must be stated as scoped to the batch {10,12,13,14}; unscoped it is false.

DROP (false as written): "Substate 12 is the only one of the four that re-evaluates anything per frame." Replace with: "Of the four, only substate 12 re-evaluates in the ARBITRATION phase. Substates 10 and 14 re-evaluate and self-transition every frame inside their EXECUTORS." Evidence: EXECUTOR[10] re-dispatches a nested 5-way FSM on +0x6 each frame (`801041b4 lbu v1,6(s1)` / `801041c0 sltiu v0,v1,0x5` / `801041c4 beq v0,zero,0x8010437c` with delay slot `801041c8 sll v0,v1,2` / `801041d4 lw v0,228(at)` table @0x801000e4 / `801041dc jr v0`), decrements a timer @+0x158 and transitions on expiry (`80104354 lhu v1,344(s1)` / `8010435c addiu v0,v1,-1` / `80104360 bne v1,zero,0x8010437c` / delay `80104364 sh v0,344(s1)` / `80104368 addiu v0,zero,4` / `8010436c j 0x8010437c` / delay `80104370 sb v0,6(s1)`), and transitions off the turn helper result (`80104254 jal 0x80015714` / `8010426c bne v0,zero,0x8010437c` / delay `80104270 sh v1,118(s1)` / `80104274 addiu v0,zero,2` / delay `8010427c sb v0,6(s1)`). EXECUTOR[14] branches on +0x6 each frame (`80104d90 lbu v1,6(s0)` / `80104d98 beq v1,zero,0x80104db4` delay `80104d9c addu s2,a2,zero` / `80104da4 beq v1,v0,0x80104dd0`) and compares +0x14D against 10 (`80104dd0 lbu v1,333(s0)` / `80104dd8 bne v1,v0,0x80104e0c`).

PORTING RULE that follows: the decision/executor split is NOT "decision = per-frame re-evaluation, executor = action". The correct model is: the decision handler's ONLY job is to overwrite +0x5 (sub_state_1) before the executor index is re-read at 0x801011d0; per-frame re-evaluation of the INNER state +0x6 lives in the executors. Do not use "empty decision" to infer "static substate".

findings.meaning: Every 32-bit store to +0x14C in this overlay is really a packed 4-byte write: byte0=clip index, byte1=start frame, byte2/3=extra. e.g. `sw 0x00070019` means clip=0x19, frame=0, +0x14E=0x07. FUN_8002959c(entity, model_ptr, anim_table_ptr, speed) advances the clip and returns non-zero exactly on the frame the clip wraps/ends. Port signature: a1=model/skeleton, a2=anim table base, a3=speed (256 or 512 in these substates).

verdict.why:
The three HEADLINE facts survive — I independently re-derived them and they are correct. But the submission's DISASSEMBLY quote is doctored and its MEANING/signature is refuted by real, reached code. Per "refuted=true if ANY part fails":

WHAT I CONFIRMED (independently proven):
- +0x14C = clip index byte: `800295a8: lbu v0,332(a0)` / `800295b0: sll v0,v0,2` / `800295b4: addu a2,a1,v0` / `800295bc: lw v1,0(a2)`. Table entry is {low u16 = frame count, high u16 = byte offset}: `800295c8: andi a2,v1,0xffff` (count) and `800295e4: srl v1,v1,16` (offset). Corroborated at `80029670: lbu v0,332(s2)` / `80029678: sll v0,v0,2` / `8002967c: addu v0,v0,a1` / `80029680: lhu s3,0(v0)`.
- +0x14D = frame index byte: `800295e8: lbu v0,333(a0)` / `800295f0: sll v0,v0,2` / `800295f4: addu a2,v1,v0`.
- +0x178 keyframe ptr: `800295f8: sw a2,376(a0)`. Confirmed.
- Return non-zero on clip end — PROVEN, and the claim never located it. It is in the callee tail, and I checked the delay slot: `80029b28: lbu v0,333(s2)` / `80029b30: addiu v0,v0,1` / `80029b34: sb v0,333(s2)` / `80029b38: andi v0,v0,0xff` / `80029b3c: sltu v0,v0,s3` / `80029b40: bne v0,zero,0x80029b50` / `80029b44: addu v0,zero,zero` (DELAY SLOT, always runs -> 0 = continue) / `80029b48: sb zero,333(s2)` / `80029b4c: addiu v0,zero,1` (wrap -> 1). Both paths reach it (`800299b8: j 0x80029b00` and `80029af8: bne t2,zero,0x800299d0` falling through to 80029b00).
- Consumer delay slot at `801048d4: beq v0,zero,0x801048e0` / `801048d8: addiu v0,zero,257` / `801048dc: sw v0,4(s0)` is assigned correctly.
- The example constant is real: `80104790: lui v0,0x7` (delay slot of `8010478c: beq v1,zero,0x801047b8`) + `801047b8: ori v0,v0,0x19` + `801047c0: sw v0,332(s0)` = sw 0x00070019.

FAILURE 1 — THE QUOTED FUNCTION BODY IS DOCTORED (decisive). The claim prints `800295bc: lw v1,0(a2)` immediately followed by `800295e4: srl v1,v1,16`, presenting straight-line fall-through. Five instructions including a CONDITIONAL BRANCH and TWO delay slots were silently deleted. Byte-confirmed via `bytes 0x800295b8 44`:
  800295b8: ff ff 02 3c = lui v0,0xffff
  800295c0: 24 10 e2 00 = and v0,a3,v0
  800295c4: 07 00 40 10 = beq v0,zero,+7 -> 0x800295e4   <-- 800295e4 is a BRANCH TARGET, not fall-through
  800295c8: ff ff 66 30 = andi a2,v1,0xffff              <-- DELAY SLOT
  800295cc: 02 1c 03 00 = srl v1,v1,16
  800295d0: 4d 01 82 90 = lbu v0,333(a0)
  800295d4: 21 18 a3 00 = addu v1,a1,v1
  800295d8: 23 10 c2 00 = subu v0,a2,v0        (count - frame)
  800295dc: 7c a5 00 08 = j 0x800295f0
  800295e0: ff ff 42 24 = addiu v0,v0,-1       <-- DELAY SLOT: count - frame - 1 = REVERSE playback
This is a second, reachable playback mode the claim erases entirely.

FAILURE 2 — "a3 = speed (256 or 512)" IS FALSE (decisive). The reverse path above is taken whenever a3 & 0xFFFF0000 != 0, and the overlay does exactly that at two sites:
  80103e00: lui a3,0x1 / 80103e04: jal 0x8002959c / 80103e08: ori a3,a3,0x100  (DELAY SLOT) -> a3 = 0x00010100
  8010a134: lui a3,0x1 / 8010a138: jal 0x8002959c / 8010a13c: ori a3,a3,0x100  (DELAY SLOT) -> a3 = 0x00010100
A port built to the claimed signature plays those two clips FORWARD instead of REVERSE. Additionally, across all 70 call sites of 0x8002959c in EMZ0.BIN, a3 is also 128 (`80109c88`, `80109cc0`) and 1024 (`8010909c`, `80107a3c`, `80106ff8`, `801069d8`, `80105f40`) — so even the literal enumeration "256 or 512" is wrong.

FAILURE 3 — "byte2/3 = extra" IS FALSE. +0x14E is a live interpolation-step countdown, not padding: `800296a8: lbu t3,334(s2)` / `800296b0: beq t3,zero,0x8002973c` gates the ENTIRE blend block; `800296b8: andi v0,a3,0xffff` / `800296bc: mult v0,t3` / `800296e4: addiu v0,zero,4096` / `800296ec: subu v0,v0,t1` forms weight = 4096 - (a3&0xffff)*[+0x14E]; and it is decremented every call at `800299c0: lbu v0,334(s2)` / `800299c8: addiu v0,v0,-1` / `800299cc: sb v0,334(s2)`. The overlay reads it (`80101500: lbu v0,334(s0)`, `801033d0: lbu v0,334(s2)`, `80103c30: lbu a0,334(s1)`) and writes it (`8010b75c: sb v0,334(s2)`). Treating byte2 as "extra" drops all inter-frame interpolation. So in `sw 0x00070019`, the 0x07 is a 7-step blend countdown, not filler.

FAILURE 4 — THE SIGNATURE'S "entity" IS UNPROVEN. FUN_8002959c reads clip/frame from a0, but the advance and the bounds check operate on a GLOBAL: `80029644: lui s2,0x800d` / `80029648: lw s2,-7376(s2)` (= *(0x800ce330)), then `80029670: lbu v0,332(s2)` (count lookup) and `80029b28/80029b34/80029b48: ...333(s2)` (the advance). Nothing in this function writes a0's +0x14D. Whether a0 == *(0x800ce330) is UNKNOWN; the writers are `800336cc`, `800339d4`, `80033b84` (`sw s0,-7376(at)`) and were not checked. A byte-true port cannot assume this away.

FAILURE 5 — wording: the function advances the FRAME (+0x14D). It never writes +0x14C, so "advances the clip" is wrong.
verdict.correction:
KEEP (proven): +0x14C = clip index (u8) indexing a 4-byte-entry table at arg a2; entry = {u16 frame_count, u16 byte_offset_to_keyframes}. +0x14D = frame index (u8). +0x178 = cached keyframe pointer (`800295f8: sw a2,376(a0)`). Return value is non-zero exactly on wrap.

CORRECT THE MODEL TO:
1) Packed word at +0x14C is byte0 = clip, byte1 = start frame, byte2 = +0x14E = INTERPOLATION STEP COUNTDOWN (gates and drives the blend; decremented per call at 0x800299c0-0x800299cc), byte3 = not yet observed in use — mark UNKNOWN rather than "extra".

2) a3 is NOT a plain speed. Its two halves are independent:
   - a3 & 0xFFFF0000 != 0 selects REVERSE frame indexing: keyframe index = frame_count - [+0x14D] - 1 (`800295c4` branch not taken -> `800295c8` count, `800295d8: subu v0,a2,v0`, `800295e0: addiu v0,v0,-1`). Used at 0x80103e04 and 0x8010a138 with a3 = 0x00010100.
   - a3 & 0x0000FFFF is the Q12 blend step, multiplied by +0x14E to form weight 4096 - step*counter (`800296b8`-`800296ec`). Observed values: 128, 256, 512, 1024, 0x0100.

3) The frame advance/wrap is:
     frame = (u8)([g]+0x14D + 1);
     if (frame < frame_count_of([g]+0x14C))  return 0;
     [g]+0x14D = 0;  return 1;
   with unsigned compare after `andi 0xff` — note frame_count == 0 makes it always wrap and return 1.

4) Resolve, do not assume: the advance targets g = *(0x800ce330), while the pointer arithmetic in FUN_8002959c uses a0. Determine whether the caller guarantees a0 == *(0x800ce330) by decoding the writers at 0x800336cc / 0x800339d4 / 0x80033b84 before porting the signature. Until then this is UNKNOWN.

5) The real work (bone unpack, 12-bit rotation blend, advance, return) is in FUN_80029614, called at `800295fc: jal 0x80029614` / `80029600: addu a0,t0,zero` (delay slot). FUN_8002959c only resolves the keyframe pointer and tail-returns the callee's v0 (`80029604`-`80029610` restore/jr with no v0 modification). Port them as two functions.

findings.title: Substate 10 is NOT an attack — it is a turn-to-angle + randomised idle/moan clip loop (clips 0..5)
findings.meaning: The task brief assumed 10 was an attack. It is not. It plays clips 0..5 (the base idle set: +0x218 is seeded to 0 or 2 by the re-init path, see EXECUTOR[13]), turns to an angle held in +0x1D4, loops random clips for (rnd&0x7F)+60 frames, then returns to WALK. There is no distance test, no player reference and no damage call anywhere in 0x8010417C..0x80104394. Byte table at 0x801000DC = {0x00, 0x02, 0x04}.
openQuestions: Semantics of +0x1D4 (low 12 bits = the target yaw, bit 0x4000 selects the clip row) — who writes it was not traced.
Semantics of +0x1D6 bit 0x8000, which case 3 mirrors from keyframe word bit 0x00010000 (0x8010433C-0x80104350).

verdict.why:
The instruction transcription and ALL delay-slot assignments in the claim are correct — I re-disassembled every quoted address and found zero transcription errors (including the tricky `8010428c: addu s0,v0,zero` sitting in the SECOND jal's delay slot and therefore capturing the FIRST rand — the claimant read that correctly). The tables are real: EXECUTOR[10] @0x8010c8f4 -> 0x8010417c; sub-table 0x801000e4 -> {0x801041e4, 0x80104234, 0x80104280, 0x801042d4, 0x80104374}; bytes @0x801000dc = `00 02 04`. The negative claim also holds: within 0x8010417c..0x80104390 the only jals are 0x80015fe8 (PRNG), 0x8002959c, 0x80015714; +0x1F0 (496) is never read; and +0x178 is provably NOT a player pointer because 0x8002959c writes it itself (`800295f8: sw a2,376(a0)`) as the current EDD keyframe pointer.

BUT the claim is marked PROVEN and fails on four points.

(1) FALSIFIED LABEL — "+0x218 = base idle clip" / "the base idle set". The WALK executor (0x80101a40, sub_state_1=1, the one already ported byte-true) sets the identical clip word from the identical field:
  80101a74: addiu v0,zero,1
  80101a78: sb v0,6(s1)
  80101a7c: lbu v0,536(s1)            ; SAME +0x218
  80101a80: lui v1,0xf
  80101a84: addu v0,v0,v1
  80101a88: jal 0x80015fe8
  80101a8c: sw v0,332(s1)             ; DELAY: +0x14C = 0x000F0000 | [+0x218]
Same field, same 0xF0000, same +0x14C, and it is then played through the same data pointers (80101ad8: lw a1,264(s1) / 80101adc: lw a2,380(s1)). A clip value that WALK plays cannot be called "the base idle clip". That is an invention, not a proof.

(2) TWO DIFFERENT ANIMATION BANKS, presented as one clip space. The claim's meaning says "It plays clips 0..5". The executor actually uses two distinct banks:
  80104238: lw a1,264(s1)   / 8010423c: lw a2,380(s1)    ; case 1 -> bank A (+0x108/+0x17C)
  801042d8: lw a1,400(s1)   / 801042dc: lw a2,404(s1)    ; case 3 -> bank B (+0x190/+0x194)
and 0x8002959c indexes the clip out of the SECOND pointer:
  800295a8: lbu v0,332(a0)    ; clip = +0x14C byte0
  800295ac: addu a1,a2,zero   ; a1 = arg2
  800295b4: addu a2,a1,v0     ; (after sll v0,v0,2) = arg2 + clip*4
So case 0/1's clip [+0x218] indexes bank A while case 2/3's clips 0..5 index bank B — different clip spaces. Neither bank pointer appears in the claim's disassembly excerpt or its constants list. A port written from this claim would feed case 3 the wrong anim data. Note also there are no stores to +0x190/+0x194 anywhere in EMZ0.BIN, so bank B is set by the EXE — its content is UNKNOWN and "idle/moan" is unsupported for it too.

(3) TURN-TO-ANGLE ASSERTED WITHOUT THE INSTRUCTIONS. The claim states "turns to an angle held in +0x1D4" but its excerpt jumps from 0x80104230 straight to 0x80104280, never showing the turn at all. The real code is 80104248: addu a0,s1,zero / 8010424c: lhu a1,468(s1) / 80104250: addiu a2,zero,32 / 80104254: jal 0x80015714 / 80104258: andi a1,a1,0xfff (DELAY), and the completion test 8010425c: lhu v1,118(s1) / 80104264: addu v1,v1,v0 / 80104268: sll v0,v0,16 / 8010426c: bne v0,zero,0x8010437c / 80104270: sh v1,118(s1) (DELAY). The turn RATE 32 is a behavior constant with no @0x citation in the claim.

  8010423c: lw a2,380(s1)          ; +0x17C
  80104240: jal 0x8002959c
  80104244: addiu a3,zero,256      ; DELAY

(3) PHASE 3 SIDE EFFECT OMITTED ENTIRELY — per-frame animation-flag propagation into +0x1D6 bit 15:
  8010432c: lhu v0,470(s1)         ; +0x1D6
  80104330: lw v1,376(s1)          ; +0x178 = frame ptr written by FUN_8002959C @0x800295f8
  80104334: andi a0,v0,0x7fff      ; clear bit15
  80104338: sh a0,470(s1)
  8010433c: lw v0,0(v1)
  80104340: lui v1,0x1
  80104344: and v0,v0,v1           ; test bit 0x10000 of the frame word
  80104348: beq v0,zero,0x80104354
  8010434c: ori v0,a0,0x8000       ; DELAY

(5) +0x14C IS A PACKED 4-BYTE FIELD, NOT A SCALAR CLIP ID.        8010132c: beq v0,zero,0x80101380    ; v1 == 0 -> skip  => requires |delta| >= 800

       80101378: sw v0,4(s0)

verdict.why: CONFIRMED by independent disassembly + byte check. (1) Instructions are real and exactly as quoted: bytes @0x80101774 = `14 05 07 24` = 0x24070514 = `addiu a3,zero,0x514`(1300); @0x80101788 = `85 55 00 0c` = jal 0x80015614; @0x8010178c = `21 98 40 00` = 0x00409821 = `addu s3,v0,zero`; @0x80101790 = `3e 02 02 92` = 0x9202023e = `lbu v0,574(s0)`. (2) Delay slots re-derived from scratch and they match: `addiu a3,zero,1024` @0x8010174c is the delay slot of jal @0x80101748 -> call#1 tol=1024; `addu s4,v0,zero` @0x8010176c is the delay slot of jal @0x80101768 -> s4 = call#1 (1024) result; `addu s3,v0,zero` @0x8010178c is the delay slot of jal @0x80101788 -> s3 = call#2 (512) result; call#3 (1300) returns into v0 which is destroyed by `lbu v0,574(s0)` @0x80101790. (3) Register census over the full function 0x80101714-0x80101a3c: exactly three `jal 0x80015614` (0x80101748/0x80101768/0x80101788), no fourth; s4 written ONLY @0x8010176c, read @0x80101864 and @0x801018ac; s3 written ONLY @0x8010178c, read @0x801017f4, @0x801019c0, @0x801019f4 — neither is ever re-assigned, so no later path can rescue the 1300 result. (4) I closed the purity gap the claim did NOT cover: its cited range 0x80015614..0x80015694 stops at the function itself, but 0x80015614 does `jal 0x800154ac` @0x80015640, which does `jal 0x8008d190` @0x80015520. I checked both: 0x8008d190's body (0x8008d190..0x8008d25c `jr ra`) contains NO jal and every store is frame-local (`sw v0,0(sp)`, `sw a0,56(sp)`, `sw zero,112(sp)`, `sw v0,4(a1)` a1=sp+4i, `sw v1,0(a3)` a3=sp+60+4i, `sw v0,0(t1)` t1=sp+116+4i; frame = 168 bytes). The `sw ra,-9348(at)` @0x8008d270 lies past the `jr ra` and belongs to a different function. So the whole call chain writes no globals and no entity fields. (5) The div-by-zero break @0x80015500 is unreachable here (guarded by `beq s0,zero,0x80015544` @0x800154ec), so the discarded call cannot even trap. (6) 64-bit-return pedantry also fails to break it: the residual v1 (`andi v1,v0,0xfff` @0x80015658) is never read after 0x80101788 — the first v1 touch on every path is a write (`lw v1,500(s0)` @0x801017a4, `lbu v1,262(s0)` @0x80101808, `lbu v1,8(s1)` @0x801018e8). Every material assertion is PROVEN; only two wording defects remain (see correction).
verdict.correction: Claim stands; three refinements, none fatal. (a) "FUN_80015614 is pure (no stores)" is literally false as worded — it DOES store: `sw s0,16(sp)` @0x80015618, `sw s1,20(sp)` @0x80015620, `sw ra,24(sp)` @0x80015634. These are callee-saved spills restored by the epilogue @0x80015684-0x80015690, so the intended meaning (no game-state side effects) is correct; the wording should say "no stores outside its own stack frame". (b) The cited evidence range was insufficient: purity must be argued over the transitive callees 0x800154ac and 0x8008d190, not just 0x80015614..0x80015694. I verified both are clean, and the stronger fact is that the chain never reaches the PRNG 0x80015fe8 — so a byte-true port may DELETE the 1300 call entirely with zero observable divergence (not merely "only if it wants cycle parity"; there is no RNG desync risk). (c) The claim states the corrected s3 mapping but leaves s4 implicit — spell it out for the port: s4 = the ±1024 cone result (a3 set in the delay slot @0x8010174c), s3 = the ±512 cone result, 1300 = dead. Also, "inverts every cone gate" is loose rhetoric: FUN_80015614 returns 0 when the player is inside the cone (`bne v0,zero,0x80015684` / `addu v0,zero,zero` @0x8001566c-0x80015670, else ±tol via @0x8001567c/@0x80015680), and the gates test `sll v0,sN,16; b(ne|eq) v0,zero` i.e. "0 = inside". A delay-slot-blind reading substitutes the WRONG TOLERANCE (s3: 512->1300, s4: 1024->512); it does not logically invert the predicate.

verdict.why:
The instruction transcription is accurate and the two hard delay slots were handled correctly, but the assertion labeled PROVEN — "exactly one of the two is ever set" — is false in two independent, port-breaking ways, and the claim misses two other writers of the same bit pair.

(1) ~50% OF THE TIME NEITHER BIT IS SET. The claim's own listing contains the gate but its MEANING sentence ignores it:
  80105e24: jal 0x80015fe8
  80105e28: nop                          (delay)
  80105e2c: andi v0,v0,0x1
  80105e30: bne v0,zero,0x80105f14
  80105e34: nop                          (delay)
0x80105f14 is `jal 0x80106310` — past the entire bit assignment. So on rand&1 != 0 the block writes NEITHER 0x20 nor 0x40. The STATUS-line claim "exactly one is set at random in the hurt path" is therefore wrong half the time; a port that always picks one would disable a reach half-sector on ~50% of zombies that should keep both.

(2) THE WRITE ITSELF DOES NOT ENFORCE EXCLUSIVITY. Path A is a pure OR that preserves a pre-existing 0x40:
  80105e50: lhu v1,538(s4)               ; reads the LIVE value
  80105e58: ori v1,v1,0x20
  80105e5c: beq s0,zero,0x80105e70
  80105e60: sh v1,538(s4)                ; delay slot: stores old|0x20 — 0x40 NOT cleared
Only path B clears the other bit (80105e64: andi v0,v1,0xffdf). So "exactly one is ever set" is an inference about global state, not something these instructions prove — yet it is labeled PROVEN. The block's ONLY entry gate is bit 0x1000 (80105e18: andi v0,v0,0x1000), NOT 0x60.

(3) THE OVERLAY ITSELF SHOWS EXCLUSIVITY IS NOT AUTOMATIC. Both OTHER writers of these bits are explicitly guarded by a 0x60 pre-check, which the claimed site lacks:
  801029ac: andi v0,v0,0x60 / 801029b0: bne v0,zero,0x80102a48
  80105288: andi v0,v1,0x60 / 8010528c: bne v0,zero,0x801053dc
The engine spends instructions enforcing "neither bit already set" at the other two sites — evidence the invariant is maintained deliberately, not implied by the claimed code.

(4) TWO OTHER WRITERS ARE MISSING ENTIRELY. Both write the same +0x21A bits on the same struct (HURT prologue 80104f48: addu s1,a0,zero; FUN_80105bc0 prologue 80105bc8: addu s4,a0,zero):

This selection is DETERMINISTIC from +0x1D0 bit 0x80 — not random — and is arguably the primary "which side" decision.
  - EXECUTOR[3] = FUN_801025ec (table 0x8010c8d8): 80102a28: ori v1,v1,0x40 stored always at 80102a34 (delay slot of beq), flipped to 0x20 at 80102a38: andi v0,v1,0xffbf / 80102a3c: ori v0,v0,0x20 when +0x23D & 0x2.
A port built from this claim alone would omit both.

(5) MISLABELED CONSTANT. "+0x21A cleared on re-init @0x801049DC": the instruction 801049dc: sh zero,538(s1) is real, but it lives in FUN_80104928 = EXECUTOR[13] (0x8010c8cc[13] -> 0x80104928), a sub_state_1==13 executor — not a generic re-init. The actual init-time clear is 8010087c: sh zero,538(s2) inside the INIT state 0x8010065C.

Bit 0 is set at exactly ONE site, 0x800402A8, reachable only when the new HP is negative (`80040264 bltz v0` for mode 1; `80040284 bgez v0` / `8004028C slti v0,v0,-14` / `800402A0 andi v0,v0,0x1000` for mode 0), and that block does `800402B0 sh zero,342(a2)` (HP=0) and `800402B4 ori v1,v1,0x1000`. Bit 0 therefore means THE PLAYER JUST DIED, not "the bite landed". Also for mode 0 the return can be 0, 1 OR 2 — and 2 is not plainly "player dead" either: 0x800402C0 is the overkill/already-dead path (`800402CC ori v1,v1,0x80` -> +0x1D3, and [0x800CFB74] |= 0x04000000).
(4) Structural omission: 0x801025EC is not only upright EXECUTOR[3]. The crawl ACTIVE variant 0x80101210 uses DIFFERENT tables (`80101240 lw v0,-14068(at)` = 0x8010C90C, `80101268 lw v0,-14056(at)` = 0x8010C918) and `0x8010C91C -> 0x801025EC`, i.e. crawl reaches it at sub_state 1. That is the ONLY way s5=1/3 (damage 5/10) are reached; porting only upright sub_state 3 makes those two rows dead code.
(5) Minor: its own listing drops `80102888 sll v1,s5,1` (the delay slot the entire 2*s5 indexing depends on, asserted but never quoted) and `80040230 j 0x80040248` (which is what makes x5 and x2 mutually exclusive).
verdict.correction:
Keep the numeric core exactly as claimed — it is byte-verified: table @0x80100014 = {frame 16, dmg 20} {frame 1, dmg 5} {frame 16, dmg 30} {frame 1, dmg 10}, copied to sp+64..71 by the lwl/lwr+swl/swr pair at 0x80102644-0x80102660, indexed by s0 = sp+64 + (s5<<1) where s5 = (+0x10E & 1) + (entity[+0x8] in {17,23} ? 2 : 0) per 0x8010266C-0x80102690, compared against the clip frame +0x14D at 0x801028A0/0x801028AC, then FUN_800401D4(dmg, s5&1) with the x1.5 (dmg<41 AND ([0x800CFB74]&0x40 OR HP>=121)) then x5 (dmg<30) else x2 (30<=dmg<60) chain, subtracting from the HP halfword at 0x800CFD4E.

Apply these corrections before porting:

1. 0x800D482A: mark UNKNOWN, not "difficulty". Cite it as "s16 rank global @0x800D482A, only two readers (0x80040218, 0x80068208), writer NOT FOUND by static immediate scan; the x5/x2 amplification applies only when it == 3 (0x8004021C addiu v0,zero,3 / 80040220 bne v1,v0,0x80040248)". Finding the writer needs a savestate/dynamic watchpoint or a base-register-relative store scan.

2. SE constant address: the id 3 is at 0x801028E8 (`addiu a0,zero,3`), not 0x801028EC. Label 0x8005BD6C as UNVERIFIED (audio-dispatch-shaped but unproven).

3. Return semantics of FUN_800401D4 (mode = s5&1):
   mode 1 (crawling): returns 1 iff (s16)newHP < 0 (0x80040264), else 0.
   mode 0 (upright): 0 if newHP >= 0 (0x80040284 -> 0x800402E8); 2 if newHP < -14 (0x8004028C) OR player+0x154 already has 0x1000 (0x800402A0) -> 0x800402C0 sets player+0x1D3 |= 0x80 and [0x800CFB74] |= 0x04000000; otherwise 1.
   Return 1 ALWAYS means the player just died (0x800402A8 zeroes HP and sets flag 0x1000). So the phase-4 transition at 0x80102910/0x80102914 is the DEATH exit, not a normal bite ending. Phase 4 is also entered on mash-escape (0x80102884 bgez -> 0x80102890/0x80102894 when +0x158, seeded 148 at 0x80102828, goes negative) — that is the "release" path.

4. A survivable bite returns 0 and both actors STAY in phase 3, so the bite re-fires every time +0x14D comes back around to the trigger frame while the mash meter lasts. Port it as "fires on the tick where frame == trigger", not "once per grab".

5. Wire the executor for BOTH entry points: upright table 0x8010C8CC[3] and crawl table 0x8010C918[1] both point at 0x801025EC (crawl ACTIVE variant 0x80101210 reads its tables from 0x8010C90C/0x8010C918 at 0x80101240/0x80101268). Otherwise the s5=1/3 rows (dmg 5 and 10) are unreachable.

findings.title: The grab is a MASH loop, not a fixed hold — meter +0x158 = 148, drains 2/frame plus 5 per input
findings.meaning: This is the structural difference from 'play clip, deal damage'. Grab clip sequence per side: 0x0B/0x0E (seize) -> 0x0C/0x0F (bite loop) -> 0x0D/0x10 (release). The struggle meter starts at 148 and loses 2 per frame plus 5 on every frame the mash predicate is true, so a non-mashing player is held ~74 frames and a fully mashing player ~21 frames. Escape and damage are NOT mutually exclusive: the meter check at 0x80102884 falls through into the damage-frame check at 0x80102898 either way, so escaping on the exact bite frame still takes the hit. The mash predicate is FUN_8001598c: ([0x800CE310] & 0x34F) != 0.
openQuestions: Which physical buttons 0x34F maps to in RE2's processed pad word at 0x800CE310 — the mask is proven, the button set is not.

verdict.why:
I re-disassembled every cited address from EMZ0.BIN / PSX.EXE and checked the raw little-endian encodings. Every quoted instruction is verbatim correct, every constant is at the quoted address, and every delay slot is assigned correctly. I could not break the claim.

1) DISPATCH CONFIRMED (the claim never showed this, I verified it). The phase byte is +0x6 and the handler table is @0x8010001C:
  80102694: lbu v1,6(s1)
  8010269c: sltiu v0,v1,0xa
  801026a0: beq v0,zero,0x80102ebc
  801026a4: sll v0,v1,2            ; DELAY (executes either way) - correct
  801026b0: lw v0,28(at)           ; table 0x8010001C
  801026b8: jr v0
Table: [0]0x801026C0 [1]0x801027D8 [2]0x80102814 [3]0x80102838 [4]0x80102968 [5]0x801029A4 [6]0x80102BE8 [7]0x80102C30 [8]0x80102C60 [9]0x80102EB4. So 0x80102814 IS phase 2, 0x80102838 IS phase 3, 0x80102968 IS phase 4. Labels correct.

2) CONSTANTS VERIFIED BY RAW BYTES.
  80102828: 94 00 02 24 = 0x24020094 = addiu v0,zero,148   -> 148 CONFIRMED
  8010282c: 58 01 22 a6 = 0xa6220158 = sh v0,0x158(s1)     -> 344 = 0x158 CONFIRMED
  80102874: fe ff 84 24 = 0x2484fffe = addiu a0,a0,-2      -> drain 2 CONFIRMED
  80102868: 80 18 02 00 = sll v1,v0,2 ; 80102870: 21 18 62 00 = addu v1,v1,v0 -> ret*5 CONFIRMED
  80102968/6c: 3c070007 / 34e70002 -> a3 = 0x00070002; 80102998: 00671821 = addu v1,v1,a3;
  801029a0: ae23014c = sw v1,0x14C(s1) -> halfword 0x14C = clip+2, halfword 0x14E = 0x0007 CONFIRMED
  80015998: 4f 03 42 30 = 0x3042034f = andi v0,v0,0x34f    -> mask 0x34F CONFIRMED

3) DELAY SLOTS CHECKED - all correct, and the one that could have been a trap is not.
  80102884: 04 00 81 04 = 0x04810004 -> REGIMM rs=a0 rt=1 = BGEZ, offset 4 -> target 0x80102898. Genuinely bgez, target correct.
  80102888: sll v1,s5,1 is the delay slot and executes on BOTH paths; the not-taken path (8010288c-80102894) does not clobber v1, so `addu s0,v0,v1` @0x8010289c is correct on both paths. The claim's "also sets up the damage index" annotation is right.
  800159a0: sltu v0,zero,v0 is the delay slot of `jr ra` -> it IS the return value. Correct.
  801029a0: sw v1,332(s1) is the delay slot of jal 0x80039514. Correctly labeled DELAY.

4) THE ONE UNPROVEN SEMANTIC POINT - I PROVED IT, AND IT FAVORS THE CLAIM. The claim called [0x800CE310] a "mash" predicate without showing it is a press-edge rather than a held-state (if it were held-state the whole "mash" reading collapses to "hold any button"). I scanned PSX.EXE for all 22 references: exactly ONE writer, 0x80039384. Its inputs:
  80039354: lui v0,0x800d
  80039358: lw v0,-7404(v0)    ; [0x800CE314]
  8003935c: lui a0,0x800d
  80039360: lw a0,-7412(a0)    ; [0x800CE30C]
  8003936c: xor v0,v0,a0
  80039370: and v0,v0,a0       ; (prev ^ cur) & cur
  80039384: sw v0,-7408(at)    ; [0x800CE310]
And [0x800CE314] is provably the PREVIOUS frame's [0x800CE30C]:
  8003918c: lui a1,0x800d / 80039190: lw a1,-7412(a1)   ; a1 = old [0x800CE30C]
  80039198: lui at,0x800d / 8003919c: sw zero,-7412(at) ; clear [0x800CE30C]
  801391b4: sw a1,0(v1)                                  ; v1 = 0x800CE314 -> prev := old cur
then the 16-iteration remap loop rebuilds the current word (800391dc: lw v0,16(a3) / 800391e4: or v0,v0,v1 / 800391e8: sw v0,16(a3), a3 = 0x800CE2FC so 16(a3) = 0x800CE30C).
=> [0x800CE310] = rising edge = NEWLY PRESSED this frame. "Mash", not "hold", is the correct word. PROVEN.

5) REGISTER ROLES - the claim asserted "player" for s3 without showing it; I verified it. s3 is a hardcoded global, not a parameter:
  80102664: lui s3,0x800d
  80102668: addiu s3,s3,-1032   ; s3 = 0x800CFBF8
and it is never rewritten before 0x80102894 (only reload is 0x80102cbc `addiu s3,zero,3`, in a later phase handler). 0x800CFBF8 is the player work struct: FUN_800401d4 (called from this very grab block @0x801028f8) hardcodes it and applies HP damage to it:
  800401dc: lui a2,0x800d / 800401e0: addiu a2,a2,-1032   ; a2 = 0x800CFBF8
  80040248: lhu v0,342(a2) / 80040250: subu a0,v0,a0 / 8004025c: sh a0,342(a2)
Also 80102710: sw s1,436(s3) writes the zombie pointer into player+0x1B4. So "player +0x6 = 4" is correct.

6) CLIP TABLE VERIFIED FROM DATA (the claim asserted 0x0B/0x0E without showing the source). The stack tables are LWL/LWR/SWL/SWR copies the disassembler printed as .word:
  8010261c: lwl v0,3(a1) / 80102620: lwr v0,0(a1) / 8010262c: swl v0,0x13(sp) / 80102630: swr v0,0x10(sp)   (a1 = 0x8010000C -> sp+16)
  8010263c: a1 = 0x80100014 -> sp+64
Data @0x8010000c: 0b 0b 0e 0e 0b 0b 0e 0e | 10 14 01 05 10 1e 01 0a
So sp+16+s5*2 = 0x0B / 0x0E. Grab clip 0x0B/0x0E CONFIRMED, hence 0x0C/0x0F and 0x0D/0x10 CONFIRMED.

7) NO HIDDEN RESET of the meter: across the whole function (0x801025EC-0x80102EBC) offset 344 is touched only at 0x8010282c (arm 148), 0x8010286c/0x8010287c (drain), 0x80102990 (cleared on release) and 0x80102dec (unrelated later phase). And v0 from `jal 0x8001598c` is not clobbered before `sll v1,v0,2` (delay slot is nop).

8) "Escape and damage not mutually exclusive" CONFIRMED structurally: bgez taken jumps to 0x80102898; the not-taken path executes 8010288c-80102894 and then falls straight into 0x80102898 (no branch). Both paths reach the frame compare `lbu v1,333(s1)` vs `lbu v0,0(s0)` @0x801028a0/a4.
verdict.correction:
Not refuted, but three things must be corrected/added before this goes into a byte-true port:

(A) OMITTED FALL-THROUGH - phase 2 also drains on its own frame. The claim presents 0x80102814 (arm) and 0x80102838 (drain) as two separate blocks, but there is NO branch between them:
  80102830: addiu v1,v1,1
  80102834: sw v1,332(s1)
  80102838: addu a0,s1,zero      <- straight-line, phase-3 body
Phase 2 sets +0x6 = 3 and then immediately executes the entire phase-3 body in the SAME frame, including the FUN_8001598c call, the drain, the sign test AND the damage-frame compare. So at the end of the arming frame the meter is already 146 (or 141 if an edge fired), not 148. A port that treats phase 2 as "arm only, drain next frame" is off by one drain tick. (Compare phase 1 @0x801027d8, which ends with an explicit `j 0x80102ebc` @0x8010280c - the author of the overlay branched away there but deliberately did not here.)

(B) "per side" is wrong - s5 has FOUR values, not two. s5 is built at:
  8010266c: lhu v0,270(s1)
  80102674: andi s5,v0,0x1
  80102670: lbu v1,8(s1) ; 8010267c: beq v1,23 ; 80102688: bne v1,17 ; 80102690: addiu s5,s5,2
So s5 in {0,1,2,3}. The clip table happens to collapse (0b 0b 0e 0e 0b 0b 0e 0e -> 0x0B,0x0E,0x0B,0x0E) so the claim's clip values survive, BUT the damage table at 0x80100014 does not: (frame, damage) = s5=0:(0x10,20) s5=1:(0x01,5) s5=2:(0x10,30) s5=3:(0x01,10), read at 801028a4 `lbu v0,0(s0)` and 801028f4 `lbu a0,1(s0)`. Entity types 17 and 23 bite for 30/10, not 20/5. Porting only "two sides" loses that.

(C) "~21 frames for a fully mashing player" is the arithmetic floor, not an achievable single-button figure - label it INFERRED. 148/7 = 21.1 is correct arithmetic, but since [0x800CE310] is a RISING EDGE (proven above), one button can set it at most every other frame (you must release to re-press), which averages 4.5/frame -> ~33 frames. Reaching ~21 requires alternating between distinct bits of the 0x34F mask on consecutive frames. Also, the non-mashing figure is 75 drain ticks, not 74: at 74 drains the meter is exactly 0 and `bgez` @0x80102884 is TAKEN (0 >= 0 keeps struggling); it goes negative on the 75th - and, per (A), the first of those ticks happens on the phase-2 frame.

findings.title: Player death during the grab hands the zombie to sub_state_1 = 6 (the devour state)
findings.meaning: Return value 2 (player killed outright: post-hit HP < -14, or +0x154 bit 0x1000 already set) promotes the zombie to state 0x0601 = ACTIVE / sub_state_1 = 6 and the player to state (...)<<8 | 6. Because the damage call passes a1 = s5 & 1, only UPRIGHT zombies (s5 = 0 or 2) can reach return 2 — the crawling path (a1 = 1) returns at most 1 and can never trigger the devour. That asymmetry is easy to miss in a port.

verdict.why:
The instruction-level decode is CORRECT (I reproduced every quoted line verbatim, delay slots included), and the crawling-asymmetry sub-claim is genuinely PROVEN. But the headline claim "Player death during the grab hands the zombie to sub_state_1 = 6" is contradicted by the code, and two labels sold as PROVEN are inventions.

(1) HEADLINE FALSE. The ORDINARY killing blow returns 1, not 2, and does NOT reach sub 6. FUN_800401d4, a1==0 path:
  80040284: bgez v0,0x800402e8        ; HP_new >= 0 -> return 0
  80040288: slti v0,v0,-14            ; DELAY
  8004028c: bne v0,zero,0x800402c0    ; overkill -> ret 2
  80040290: addiu v0,zero,2           ; DELAY
  80040294: lhu v0,340(a2)            ; [0x800d0154]
  8004029c: andi v0,v0,0x1000
  800402a0: bne v0,zero,0x800402c0    ; ALREADY flagged -> ret 2
  800402a4: addiu v0,zero,2           ; DELAY
  800402a8: lhu v1,340(a2)            ; <-- THE NORMAL DEATH FALLS HERE
  800402ac: addiu v0,zero,1           ; ret = 1
  800402b0: sh zero,342(a2)           ; HP := 0
  800402b4: ori v1,v1,0x1000          ; set the dead flag
  800402b8: j 0x800402ec
  800402bc: sh v1,340(a2)             ; DELAY
Return values are the exact enum {0,1,2} — never 3 — so bit0 and bit1 are mutually exclusive. Back in the caller, return 1 takes the bit-0 branch and then EXITS:
  80102904: andi v0,v1,0x1
  80102908: beq v0,zero,0x80102920
  8010290c: addiu v0,zero,4           ; DELAY
  80102910: sb v0,6(s1)               ; zombie sub_state_2 = 4  (sub_state_1 STAYS 3)
  80102914: sb v0,6(s3)
  80102918: addiu v0,zero,1
  8010291c: sb v0,362(s3)
  80102920: andi v0,v1,0x2            ; 1 & 2 == 0
  80102924: beq v0,zero,0x80102ebc    ; -> epilogue, sub 6 NEVER reached
So the player dying in the grab keeps the zombie in sub_state_1 = 3 / sub_state_2 = 4. sub_state_1 = 6 requires a SECOND lethal hit on an already-dead player (bit 0x1000 set by a previous 800402a8) or an overkill blow of HP_new <= -15.

(2) "instant-death threshold HP < -14" MISLABELS the constant. Both branches out of `80040284: bgez` are lethal (HP_new < 0). `80040288: slti v0,v0,-14` does not decide life vs death — it only selects the overkill/eaten presentation over the normal collapse at 800402a8.

(3) "the devour state" is an UNPROVEN LABEL sold as PROVEN. Executor[6] = 0x80103954 (0x8010c8e4 -> 0x80103954) only proves: motion word 0x000F0018 (80103990 lui v0,0xf / 801039b0 ori v0,v0,0x18 / 801039c8 sw v0,332(s0)), one call `801039d0: jal 0x80015b94` with `801039b8: addiu a0,a0,-1032` (a0 = the player), a random moan 10/11 (801039d8 jal 0x80015fe8 / 801039f0 jal 0x8005bd6c), then at sub_state_2==2 it hands off: `801039a4: addiu v1,zero,2049` (DELAY) / `80103a48: sw v1,4(s0)` = 0x801 = ACTIVE / sub_state_1 = 8, plus `80103a4c: ori v0,v0,0x4000` into +0x10E. Nothing in the code names it "devour", and the actual multi-frame loop lives in sub_state_1 = 8 (0x80103b74, its own 9-entry table @0x801000b4).

(4) The return-2 condition is stated INCOMPLETELY as a port spec: "post-hit HP < -14, or +0x154 bit 0x1000 already set" omits the gate `80040284: bgez v0,0x800402e8`. Implementing it literally (`if (hp < -14 || (f & 0x1000)) return 2;`) is wrong whenever hp_new >= 0.
verdict.correction:
CONFIRMED PARTS (independently reproduced, keep these):
- The enclosing function is EXECUTOR entry [3] @0x801025ec (0x8010c8d8 -> 0x801025ec; decision[3] = 0x801025e4 = bare `jr ra`). Prologue 801025f4: addu s1,a0,zero (s1 = zombie), 80102664/80102668: lui s3,0x800d / addiu s3,s3,-1032 = 0x800cfbf8 (s3 = player). So `sw v0,4(a0)` with a0=s1 IS the zombie, and 0x800cfbfc IS player+4 (same struct FUN_800401d4 uses: 800401e0: addiu a2,a2,-1032). Cross-check on the byte layout: 8010257c: addiu v0,zero,257 / 80102580: sw v0,4(s0) = 0x101 = ACTIVE/WALK, so 0x601 = ACTIVE / sub_state_1 = 6, sub_state_2 = 0. CORRECT.
- Delay slots all correctly assigned by the claim (80102928 for the beq, 80102938 for the jal, 80040288/80040290/800402a4 in the EXE). CORRECT.
- The 0x601 store survives the call: FUN_80015910 is a pure leaf — 80015910: lh v0,118(a1) / 80015914: lh v1,118(a0) / 8001591c: subu / 80015920: addiu v0,v0,1024 / 80015924: andi v0,v0,0xfff / 80015928: jr ra / 8001592c: slti v0,v0,2048 (DELAY). It returns 0/1 (a facing-side flag off +0x76) and touches no memory. So the "f" in (f<<8)|6 is a 0/1 left/right variant selector, not an opaque value.
- The CRAWLING ASYMMETRY IS PROVEN, and more strongly than the claim argued. a1 = s5&1 (801028fc, DELAY of 801028f8 jal 0x800401d4), and s5 = (+0x10E)&1 (+2 if type is 0x17/0x11): 8010266c: lhu v0,270(s1) / 80102674: andi s5,v0,0x1 / 8010267c: beq v1,v0,0x80102690 / 80102690: addiu s5,s5,2. Bit0 of +0x10E is the crawl selector, proven by the ACTIVE table: 0x8010c854 -> 0x8010118c (upright), 0x8010c858 -> 0x80101210 (crawling), 0x8010c85c -> 0x8010118c, 0x8010c860 -> 0x80101210 (index = +0x10E & 0x3f, 8010115c: andi v0,v0,0x3f). Independent corroboration: the per-variant record fetched at 8010289c (s0 = sp+64 + s5*2) comes from the unaligned copy of 0x80100014, whose bytes are `10 14 01 05 10 1e 01 0a` -> s5=0: frame 0x10/dmg 20, s5=1: frame 0x01/dmg 5, s5=2: frame 0x10/dmg 30, s5=3: frame 0x01/dmg 10. Odd s5 (crawling) does 5-10 damage and, per the a1==1 path (80040258: bne a1,v0 / 80040264: bltz v0,0x800402a8 / 8004026c: j 0x800402ec), can only ever return 0 or 1 — never 2. So crawlers can never reach sub 6.

CORRECTED STATEMENT OF THE MECHANISM:
Grab executor sub_state_1 = 3 (0x801025ec), sub_state_2 = 3 block: when the anim frame +0x14D equals the per-variant trigger byte (801028a0/801028a4/801028ac), it calls FUN_800401d4(dmg = sp[64+s5*2+1], a1 = s5&1) at 801028f8.
  ret 0 -> nothing.
  ret 1 (PLAYER JUST DIED: HP_new < 0, not overkill, not already flagged; 800402a8 sets HP=0 and +0x154 |= 0x1000)
      -> zombie +0x6 = 4, player +0x6 = 4, player +0x16A = 1 (80102910/80102914/8010291c), then exit. Zombie STAYS in sub_state_1 = 3. This is the normal player-death-in-grab presentation.
  ret 2 (PLAYER ALREADY DEAD — +0x154 bit 0x1000 set by an earlier hit — OR overkill HP_new <= -15, both only when HP_new < 0)
      -> 80102930: addiu v0,zero,1537 / 80102938: sw v0,4(s1) = zombie ACTIVE / sub_state_1 = 6; player+4 = (side<<8)|6 (8010293c/80102948/80102950); global [0x800cfb74] |= 0x100 (80102944/80102954/8010295c, meaning UNKNOWN — do not invent one).
Sub_state_1 = 6 (0x80103954) is a 3-step post-death state (motion 0x000F0018, one 0x80015b94 call on the player, moan 10/11), which at sub_state_2 == 2 promotes to sub_state_1 = 8 (0x80103b74, 9-entry sub table @0x801000b4) and sets +0x10E |= 0x4000. Call state 6 "post-death handoff" and state 8 "the loop"; "devour" is a guess until the motion id 0x000F0018 is resolved against the EMD/anim catalogue.
Also note FUN_800401d4's damage pre-scaling before the HP subtract, which the claim omitted entirely: +50% if [0x800cfb74]&0x40 or [0x800cfd4e] < 121 and dmg < 41 (800401e4-80040210), and if [0x800d482a] == 3 then x5 for dmg < 30 else x2 for dmg < 60 (80040218-80040244). A byte-true port needs these before the 342(a2) subtract at 80040250.

findings.title: The WALK state can trigger the grab DIRECTLY, without ever entering substate 12 (dist < 1200)
findings.meaning: Critically for a port: substate 12 is NOT the only route into the grab. The WALK decision itself runs the identical two-half-sector reach test at dist < 1200 (vs 1300 during substate 12) with no clip-frame window, and writes 0x0301 directly. verdict.why:
I re-disassembled every cited address from EMZ0.BIN/PSX.EXE. Much of the claim IS confirmed, but it fails on four checkable points, one of them factually false.

=== FAILURE 1 (hard, factual): "Three entry paths" is WRONG — there are SIX, in TWO decision functions ===
Scanning EMZ0.BIN for `addiu rX,zero,3585` (0x24020E01) gives exactly six sites:
  801017dc, 80101828, 801019e0  <- decision[1] FUN_80101714 (the three the claim found)
  80102044, 80102090, 80102200  <- NEVER EXAMINED BY THE CLAIM
Table @0x8010c88c: [2] -> 0x80101f7c, [3] -> 0x801025e4, so all three extra sites lie inside DECISION[2] @0x80101f7c. They are real stores, not dead immediates:
  80102040: bne v0,zero,0x80102050
  80102044: addiu v0,zero,3585        ; DELAY
  80102048: j 0x8010223c
  8010204c: sw v0,4(s0)               ; <- substate 14 entry
  8010208c: bne v0,zero,0x80102098
  80102090: addiu v0,zero,3585        ; DELAY
  80102094: sw v0,4(s0)               ; <- substate 14 entry
  801021fc: bne v0,zero,0x80102208
  80102200: addiu v0,zero,3585        ; DELAY
  80102204: sw v0,4(s0)               ; <- substate 14 entry
Decision[2] repeats the identical gate structure (801021d4 lbu v0,574(s0); 80101ff8 lbu v0,574(s0); 8010200c lw v1,500(s0); 80102028 sltiu v0,v0,0x7d0; 80102038 jal 0x80015714 / 8010203c addiu a2,zero,256). A port built from the claim would miss half the entry conditions.

=== FAILURE 2 (semantic): paths (b) and (c) are NOT committed transitions ===
Path (a) is final because of an instruction the claim never quoted:
  801017e0: j 0x80101a1c
  801017e4: sw v0,4(s0)               ; DELAY — jumps PAST everything below
Paths (b)/(c) store and FALL THROUGH, and the same function then overwrites +0x4:
  8010182c: sw v0,4(s0)   (0x0E01)  -> falls into 80101830: lh v0,468(s0)
  80101854: addiu v0,zero,2561      ; DELAY of 80101850 beq
  80101858: sw v0,4(s0)             ; 0x0A01 = substate 10, CLOBBERS 0x0E01
  8010189c: addiu v0,zero,3073 / 801018a0: sw v0,4(s0)   ; 0x0C01 = substate 12
  801018e0: addiu v0,zero,3073 / 801018e4: sw v0,4(s0)
  801019e4: sw v0,4(s0)   (0x0E01)  -> falls into 801019e8
  80101a04: lui v1,0x6 (DELAY) / 80101a0c: ori v1,v1,0x801 / 80101a10: sw v1,4(s0)  ; 0x00060801
So (b) and (c) are provisional; only (a) guarantees substate 14.

=== FAILURE 3 (evidence rule): the entering instruction is never quoted ===
The claim's constants point at the `addiu` sites (801017dc / 80101828 / 801019e0), never at the `sw v0,4(s0)` that actually performs the transition (801017e4 / 8010182c / 801019e4). Its quoted listing also silently drops 801017c4 `beq v0,zero,0x801017e8` (delay 801017c8 addu a0,s0,zero), 801017b4/801017b8 (`lui v0,0x3fff` / `ori v0,v0,0xffff`, the delay slot + mask build), and 801017e8/801017f0 (path b's own cooldown re-check).

=== FAILURE 4 (unproven labels sold as PROVEN) ===
(a) "SE id 5": the claim shows zero disassembly of 0x8005bd6c. I disassembled it:
  8005bd90: lw v0,0(s2)          ; s2 = a1 = the entity
  8005bd98: andi v0,v0,0x2000
  8005bd9c: beq v0,zero,0x8005bda8
  8005bda0: addu s4,a0,zero      ; DELAY -> id = 5
  8005bda4: addiu s4,a0,16       ; id = 21 when flag 0x2000 set
  8005bda8: andi v0,s4,0xff
so the effective id is 5 OR 21, not simply 5. The function contains no SPU/sound API call in its body; it fills a queue record with the entity position (8005bff0 lw v0,56(s2) / 8005bffc lw v0,60(s2) / 8005c008 lw v0,64(s2)) — consistent with a positional SE request, but "sound" is INFERRED, not proven.
(b) "60-frame cooldown": the claim cites no decrementer at all. I found it (so the substance survives): 80100470 lbu v0,574(s0) / 80100478 beq v0,zero,0x80100484 / 8010047c addiu v0,v0,-1 (DELAY) / 80100480 sb v0,574(s0), inside the function at 0x801002c0. But "per FRAME" is still UNPROVEN: there is no jal/j and no data word anywhere in EMZ0.BIN or PSX.EXE targeting 0x801002c0; it is only installed as a pointer by 8001b288 lui v0,0x8010 / 8001b28c addiu v0,v0,704 into 0x800d001c..0x800d0058.
(c) "sw v0,332(s0) ; CLIP 0x11" mislabels a 4-byte store as a clip index. Proven: the clip index is the BYTE at +0x14C (800295a8 lbu v0,332(a0)); +0x14D is the frame counter (800295e8 lbu v0,333(a0); incremented 80029b30 addiu v0,v0,1 / 80029b34 sb v0,333(s2)); +0x14E is a separate field (800296a8 lbu t3,334(s2) / 800296b0 beq t3,zero,...). The one store therefore also resets the frame counter to 0 (which is why the frame-10 test cannot fire on the entry tick) and sets +0x14E = 0x0F. The upper half is per-clip data, not a constant — executor[12] proves it: 80104790 lui v0,0x7 / 801047b8 ori v0,v0,0x19 / 801047c0 sw v0,332(s0) = 0x00070019.
(d) Its listing jumps from 80104da4 `beq v1,v0,0x80104dd0` straight to "--- phase 0" at 80104db4, omitting 80104dac `j 0x80104e30` (delay 80104db0 nop). As quoted, sub_state_2 >= 2 would fall into phase 0 and re-arm the clip; in reality it exits.

=== WHAT I DID CONFIRM (so this is a partial, not total, refutation) ===
- table @0x8010c904 -> 0x80104d74 = executor[14]; decision[14] @0x8010c8c4 -> 0x80104d6c is just `jr ra / nop`.
- Every quoted constant is byte-exact: 80104db4 `0f 00 02 3c` lui v0,0xf; 80104db8 `11 00 42 34` ori 0x11; 80104dbc `4c 01 02 ae` sw +0x14C; 80104dc8 `0b 00 02 24` = 11; 80104dcc `44 01 02 a6` sh +0x144; 80104dd0 `4d 01 03 92` lbu +0x14D; 80104e28 `3c 00 02 24` = 60; 80104e2c `3e 02 02 a2` sb +0x23E.
- Every delay slot the claim DID mark is correct: 80104d9c, 80104ddc, 80104df8, 80104e20 (v0=1 set after the branch condition is evaluated — the tricky one, and they got it right), 801017a0, 801017d4, 801017dc, 801017fc, 80101828.
- The subtlest delay-slot call is also right: 8010178c `addu s3,v0,zero` is the delay slot of the jal at 80101788, so s3 = the result of the PREVIOUS call (8010176c a3=512), hence "+-45 deg" (512/4096*360) is the correct reading, not 1300.
- 0x80015714 returns 0 iff |a1 - entity.yaw| < a2 (80015730 sll v0,a2,1 / 80015734 slt v0,a1,v0 / 8001573c addu v0,zero,zero), so "within +-256 of +0x1F8" is right, and +0x76 is indeed yaw (turn helper 800155b0 lhu a1,118(s1)).
- Clip-end semantics of 0x8002959c -> 0x80029614 proven: 80029b3c sltu v0,v0,s3 / 80029b40 bne / 80029b44 addu v0,zero,zero (DELAY, "still playing") / 80029b48 sb zero,333(s2) / 80029b4c addiu v0,zero,1 ("ended").
- Path (c) trigger: 801018e8 lbu v1,8(s1) / 801018ec addiu v0,zero,15 / 801018f0 beq v1,v0,0x801019b4 — player +0x8 == 15, exactly as claimed.
- FUN_8001bf10 is a pool allocator: 8001bf10 addiu t2,zero,96 / 8001bf70-8001bf8c scan stride -124 over 0x800d8cf0 for a free `lhu 0(...)`==0 slot / 8001bf94 j 0x8001c21c with 8001bf98 addiu v0,zero,255 on failure — so "spawn" is defensible, and the claim was honest that it did not prove WHAT is spawned.

Substate 14 executor @0x80104D74 (table [14] @0x8010C904; decision[14] @0x8010C8C4 = 0x80104D6C is an empty `jr ra`).

Phase gate: 80104d90 lbu v1,6(s0); 80104d98 beq v1,zero,0x80104db4 (DELAY 80104d9c addu s2,a2,zero); 80104da4 beq v1,v0(=1),0x80104dd0; ELSE 80104dac `j 0x80104e30` — sub_state_2 >= 2 exits immediately.

Phase 0 (80104db4-80104dcc) writes ONE 32-bit word 0x000F0011 to +0x14C (80104dbc sw v0,332(s0)), which sets FOUR fields: clip index byte +0x14C = 0x11, frame counter +0x14D = 0 (this is what makes the frame-10 test safe on the entry tick), +0x14E = 0x0F. The upper half is per-clip data, not a constant (cf. executor[12]: 80104790 lui v0,0x7 / 801047b8 ori v0,v0,0x19 -> 0x00070019). Also 80104dc8/80104dcc: +0x144 = 11 (same value executor[12] writes at 80104824/80104828; its only reader is 801005b0 lh v0,324(s0) / 801005b8 slti v0,v0,11, gated by (+0x14D & 0xF)==1 at 801005a4, calling 0x8010c0f8 — the >=11 threshold, not proven to be "step magnitude").

Then FUN_8005bd6c(a0=5, a1=entity): the callee remaps the id to 5+16=21 when the entity's flags word bit 0x2000 is set (8005bd90-8005bda4); it queues a record carrying the entity's x/y/z (8005bff0/8005bffc/8005c008). "Positional SE request" is INFERRED — no SPU call proven.

Exit (80104e14 jal 0x8002959c, a3=256): return != 0 means the clip wrapped (80029b3c/80029b48/80029b4c). Then 80104e20 addiu v0,zero,1 (DELAY) / 80104e24 sw v0,4(s0) -> state word 1 = ACTIVE, sub_state_1 = 0; 80104e28/80104e2c -> +0x23E = 60. +0x23E is decremented once per call of the function at 0x801002c0 (80100470 lbu / 80100478 beq / 8010047c addiu -1 DELAY / 80100480 sb); that function has NO direct jal anywhere in EMZ0.BIN or PSX.EXE — it is installed as a pointer at 8001b288/8001b28c into 0x800d001c..0x800d0058, so "60 FRAMES" is UNPROVEN (it is 60 ticks of whatever calls that slot).

 DECISION[1] FUN_80101714 (WALK):

NOT FINAL — falls through to 80101830 and can be clobbered by 80101858 (0x0A01 = substate 10), 801018a0/801018e4 (0x0C01 = substate 12) or 80101a10 (0x00060801 = substate 8).
  (c) 801019e0/801019e4 — reached from 801018e8-801018f0 when player+0x8 == 15; requires +0x23E == 0, s3 == 0, +0x1F0 < 2000, player+0x1D3 == 0. NOT FINAL — falls through to 801019e8 and can be clobbered by 80101a10.
 DECISION[2] FUN_80101F7C (table [2] @0x8010c894, ends before [3] = 0x801025e4) — MISSING FROM THE CLAIM:
  (d) 80102044/8010204c — same +0x1F4 / 2000 / +-256 test (80102004-8010203c). FINAL: 80102048 `j 0x8010223c`.
  (e) 80102090/80102094 — 80102050 lbu +0x23E ... 80102084 lbu v0,467(s1) / 8010208c bne. NOT FINAL.
  (f) 80102200/80102204 — 801021d4 lbu +0x23E / 801021e0 sll v0,s3,16 / 801021e8 sltiu v0,s2,0x7d0 / 801021f4 lbu v0,467(s1). NOT FINAL (falls into 80102208).

And +0x108/+0x17C vs +0x190/+0x194 really are distinct struct fields: the EXE copy routine copies them independently — "8001ae7c: sw v0,380(s0)" / "8001ae88: sw v0,264(s0)" vs "8001aec4: sw v0,404(s0)" / "8001aed0: sw v0,400(s0)".

=== THE REFUTATION ===
The claim's whole frame is "there are two banks: the normal one (which it labels +0x108 'model ptr' / +0x17C 'anim table') and a SECOND one (+0x190/+0x194)", with substates 12/13/14 using "the (a1,a2) the ACTIVE dispatcher passed down". I traced (a1,a2) to its origin. The zombie root state dispatcher is at 0x801004C8 (found via the only reference to state table 0x8010C830 in either binary: "801004d8: lui at,0x8011" + "801004e0: lw v0,-14288(at)"):
  801004c8: lw a1,384(s0)          ; a1 = entity + 0x180   <-- NOT +0x108
  801004cc: lbu v0,4(s0)
  801004d0: lw a2,388(s0)          ; a2 = entity + 0x184   <-- NOT +0x17C
  801004d4: sll v0,v0,2
  801004d8: lui at,0x8011
  801004dc: addu at,at,v0
  801004e0: lw v0,-14288(at)       ; 0x8010c830 state table
  801004e4: nop
  801004e8: jalr v0
  801004ec: addu a0,s0,zero        ; DELAY - a0 = entity
That pair propagates unchanged through ACTIVE (0x8010114C passes a1/a2 through untouched) and the upright variant (0x8010119C addu s1,a1,zero / 0x801011C8 addu s2,a2,zero in the jalr delay slot / re-emitted at 0x801011D4 and 0x801011F0).

So (a1,a2) = (+0x180, +0x184) — a THIRD, independent pointer pair, distinct from BOTH pairs the claim discusses. The EXE loader proves they are five separate directory entries off one base s2, not aliases:
  8001aba0: sw v1,444(s1)   ; dir[0] -> +0x1BC
  8001abb0: sw v1,380(s1)   ; dir[1] -> +0x17C
  8001abc0: sw v1,264(s1)   ; dir[2] -> +0x108
  8001abd0: sw v1,388(s1)   ; dir[3] -> +0x184
  8001abe0: sw v1,384(s1)   ; dir[4] -> +0x180
(each preceded by its own "lw v1,N(s0)" + "addu v1,s2,v1" at 0x8001AB94-0x8001ABDC — different header words, different resulting pointers.)

This breaks two things:
1. "SECOND animation bank" is a miscount. +0x190/+0x194 is not the second of two; the executor-handed bank (+0x180/+0x184) is a separate one again. The constants list labelling +0x108 "model ptr" and +0x190 "second model ptr" encodes that wrong two-bank model.
2. The actionable conclusion is wrong in a way that would ship a bug: "a port that resolves all of them against one animation bank will play the wrong clips for substate 10 case 3 while looking correct for 12 and 14." Case 1 is ALSO wrong. "80104238: lw a1,264(s1)" (+0x108) is not the +0x180 the dispatcher handed down, so substate 10 case 1 deviates from substates 12/13/14 exactly as much as case 3 does. A port implementing this claim fixes case 3 and leaves case 1 silently resolving against the wrong table, because the claim presents case 1 as the baseline.

Secondary defect: the block headed "EXECUTOR[12] / [13] / [14]" cites only two call sites — 0x80104854 (inside executor[12], 0x80104748) and 0x80104E0C (inside executor[14], 0x80104D74). Nothing from executor[13] (0x80104928-0x80104D73) is quoted, so [13] is asserted without evidence. It happens to be true — I found "80104938: addu s3,a1,zero" / "80104940: addu s4,a2,zero" and the use at "80104a6c: addu a1,s3,zero" / "80104a70: addu a2,s4,zero" / "80104a74: addiu a3,zero,256" / "80104a78: jal 0x8002959c" — but the claim did not show it, and its speed summary ("256 for substate 10 and 14, 512 for substate 12") omits [13]'s 256 @0x80104A74.
verdict.correction:
Corrected statement, with the bank identities actually resolved:

The RE2 zombie entity holds SEVERAL independent (model, anim-table) pointer pairs, installed by the EXE loader at 0x8001AB94-0x8001ABE0 from distinct directory entries of one base (s2):
  dir[0] -> +0x1BC   (8001aba0: sw v1,444(s1))
  dir[1] -> +0x17C   (8001abb0: sw v1,380(s1))
  dir[2] -> +0x108   (8001abc0: sw v1,264(s1))
  dir[3] -> +0x184   (8001abd0: sw v1,388(s1))
  dir[4] -> +0x180   (8001abe0: sw v1,384(s1))
plus +0x190/+0x194, written by a separate EXE routine ("80018f6c: sw t1,400(a0)" / "80018f7c: sw v0,404(v1)").

The pair handed to every state handler is (+0x180, +0x184), set at the root dispatcher:
  801004c8: lw a1,384(s0)     ; +0x180
  801004d0: lw a2,388(s0)     ; +0x184
  801004e8: jalr v0           ; state table 0x8010C830, index = entity+0x4
  801004ec: addu a0,s0,zero   ; DELAY
and passed through ACTIVE (0x8010114C) and the upright variant (0x8010118C: s1=a1 @0x8010119C, s2=a2 @0x801011C8 in the jalr delay slot, re-emitted @0x801011D4/0x801011F0) to the executor.

Given that, the correct picture of substate 10 (executor 0x8010417C) is:

- Executor[10] uses NONE of the handed (a1,a2). PROVEN: its prologue saves only "80104184: addu s1,a0,zero"; a1 is destroyed at "80104190: lui a1,0x8010" before any read; a2 is never read. Every animation call in it re-loads pointers from the entity.
- Case 1 (0x80104234) animates from (+0x108, +0x17C) at speed 256 — a DIFFERENT pair from the handed (+0x180, +0x184).
- Case 3 (0x801042D4) animates from (+0x190, +0x194) at speed 256 — a THIRD pair, different from both.
- Substates 12 (0x80104748), 13 (0x80104928) and 14 (0x80104D74) DO use the handed pair, i.e. (+0x180, +0x184):
    12: 80104854 addu a1,s1,zero / 80104858 addu a2,s2,zero / 80104864 addiu a3,zero,512 / 8010486c jal 0x8002959c / 80104870 sh v0,118(s0) [DELAY]
        and 801048c4/801048c8 + 801048cc jal / 801048d0 addiu a3,zero,512 [DELAY]
    13: 80104a6c addu a1,s3,zero / 80104a70 addu a2,s4,zero / 80104a74 addiu a3,zero,256 / 80104a78 jal 0x8002959c   (s3=a1 @0x80104938, s4=a2 @0x80104940)
    14: 80104e0c addu a1,s1,zero / 80104e10 addu a2,s2,zero / 80104e14 jal 0x8002959c / 80104e18 addiu a3,zero,256 [DELAY]
        (s1=a1 @0x80104D84, s2=a2 @0x80104D9C - the latter in the delay slot of "80104d98: beq v1,zero,0x80104db4", so it always executes)

PORTING CONSEQUENCE: a port must resolve BOTH of substate 10's cases against their own banks, not just case 3. Clip indices used under substate 10 are meaningless against the (+0x180,+0x184) table that 12/13/14 use.

INFERRED (not proven): that these pointer pairs are "model + animation table" in the EMD sense. What is PROVEN about the consumer 0x8002959c is only its indexing arithmetic: it reads the clip selector as a byte at entity+0x14C ("800295a8: lbu v0,332(a0)"), scales it by 4 and indexes a2 ("800295b0: sll v0,v0,2" / "800295b4: addu a2,a1,v0" — note a1 was reloaded from a2 at 0x800295AC — / "800295bc: lw v1,0(a2)"), uses a second byte at entity+0x14D ("800295d0: lbu v0,333(a0)") as a frame bias when (a3 & 0xFFFF0000) != 0, stores the resolved entry to entity+0x178 ("800295f8: sw a2,376(a0)") and calls 0x80029614 with a0 = the FIRST pointer ("800295fc: jal 0x80029614" / "80029600: addu a0,t0,zero" [DELAY], t0 = original a1 from "800295a0: addu t0,a1,zero"). So arg2 is a table indexed by the clip selector and arg1 is data consumed by 0x80029614; the finer semantics are UNKNOWN without disassembling 0x80029614.

Also UNKNOWN: what distinguishes the +0x190/+0x194 pair semantically (its writer at 0x80018F6C stores original_a0+4 from "80018f38: addiu t1,a0,4", i.e. a pointer into a caller-supplied buffer rather than the same directory the other pairs come from). That difference is real but its meaning needs the caller of 0x80018E44-0x80018FAC traced.
